rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 573.5, best so far). The oval finished 20/20 with rms 0.011 m, so the steering gains and sensor geometry work on gentle curves. The s-bend finished 12/20 with 8 off-track exits and progress 0.92. The slalom failed in all 20 trials (progress 0.19, 0.5 line-loss events per trial, off_track every time). Steering oscillation is moderate (0.18 to 0.39) and not jittering. The failures are on fast direction changes and on bends where the robot drifts past the 0.06 m limit before it can correct. Speed is the most likely cause. At base_speed 1.5 the robot has large lateral momentum when it enters a reversal, and the rear sensors lose the tape. The oval has time margin (finish time 1.87 s against a 3 s limit), so a slower base speed still finishes. Change: lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3 (about 65 percent PWM). Everything else stays fixed (7 sensors, y 0.08 m, footprint 0.016 m, weights, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 1.0, last_direction) so the effect of speed can be read cleanly. Expected result: oval still completes, with finish time about 2.1 s, costing roughly 3 to 4 score points on the time term. The s-bend should finish 14 or more of 20, slalom progress should rise above 0.35, and line-loss events should fall. Hypotheses: (a) if slalom still goes off track with progress under 0.3, speed is not the main limit and kp must rise (to about 3.5) to give more steering authority on reversals; (b) if oval completion_time exceeds 2.3 s or the oval stops finishing, base_speed should return to about 1.4; (c) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.4, kd should come down toward 0.8. Measurements wanted next: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort.
